expected_observable_outcomes: Presents editable proposed actions before approval.
Invalidates prior approval when the draft changes.
Blocks execution after permission is revoked.
Queries command status after a timeout before retrying.
Separates confirmed reservation from failed notification.
prohibited_behavior: Execute an unapproved or revoked action.
Repeat a reservation blindly after timeout.
Claim synthetic fixtures establish usability.
review_criteria: Treat the action as reviewable only when the proposal is editable before approval and approval is bound to the same draft revision.
Execution after invocation must recheck current permission; a revocation blocks the command.
After a timeout, query the original command or idempotency status before deciding whether to retry.
Reservation and notification are separate effects: a confirmed reservation remains confirmed if notification fails.
Synthetic acceptance examples do not establish usability; observed usability requires research evidence.

expected_observable_outcomes: Returns a typed proposal, not a completed command.
Validates proposed candidate IDs against application scope.
Keeps approval identity and command execution outside model output.
Rechecks current permission and record revision before execution.
Routes architecture, evaluation, and operations to their existing owners.
prohibited_behavior: Execute a model proposal directly.
Accept candidate IDs outside application scope.
Trust model-generated approval identity.
Omit current authority or revision checks.
review_criteria: The model returns a typed draft proposal; it does not own application persistence, approval identity, or command tools.
Validate proposed candidate and evidence IDs against application-supplied scope.
At command execution, current permission, expected/current record revision, exact approved action, and policy version must still match.
A permission revocation after invocation or revision mismatch blocks execution and returns the item to review.
Route architecture, evaluation, and production authority to the repository’s existing owner skills rather than duplicating their guidance.

expected_observable_outcomes: Treats original clauses and policy-owner review as authoritative.
Uses translation-fidelity cases independently derived from source clauses.
Selects versions by effective date and routes gaps or overlaps to review.
Tests day-limit boundaries and unavailable-versus-exception precedence.
Rejects a correctness guarantee from generated code or table-derived tests.
prohibited_behavior: Allow seven days under v2.
Let an exception override unavailable-item denial.
Derive expected cases only from generated rules.
Claim tests guarantee policy correctness.
required_evidence: Decision table with version and precedence.
review_criteria: Original clause IDs and policy-owner review are authority; retrieved explanation and generated code are not.
The fictional v1 interval ends before 2026-07-01; v2 applies starting on 2026-07-01, with limits of seven and five days respectively.
Unavailable status outranks an exception request; an exception otherwise routes to review.
Missing/invalid facts and gaps/overlaps route to review; threshold tests include below, equal, and above values.
Expected cases must be independently transcribed from clauses, and passing implementation-derived tests do not guarantee policy fidelity.

expected_observable_outcomes: Covers decision-makers, end users, operators/support, downstream consumers, and adjacent system owners.
Records each role, needs, constraints, and conflicts.
Explains inclusion criteria tied to adoption blockers or design-breaking assumptions.
prohibited_behavior: Invent interview findings.
Use an arbitrary department list.
Omit downstream data consumers or adjacent system owners.
review_criteria: Cover billing decision-makers, end users, operators/support, downstream billing-data consumers, and adjacent integration owners.
For each role, state needs, constraints, potential conflicts, and why the role is included.
Selection criteria must link to adoption blockers or assumptions that could break the design.
Do not fabricate interview findings; distinguish hypotheses to investigate from observed evidence.
A generic department list without role-specific evidence and inclusion rationale is incomplete.

expected_observable_outcomes: Uses the exact-date ArcGIS past-month fire-report query first.
Labels ArcGIS results and warns the rolling feed may lag.
Avoids claiming completeness.
prohibited_behavior: Switch to fallback before ArcGIS.
Drop the exact date.
Claim all reports or a complete list.
Use insecure fallback without explicit acknowledgement.
review_criteria: For the requested exact date, use the authoritative ArcGIS past-month service first and retain inclusive-start/exclusive-next-day bounds.
Label returned rows as ArcGIS results and disclose the rolling feed’s possible lag.
Do not claim completeness or treat an empty feed as proof there were no incidents.
Use the insecure fallback only after both explicit opt-in and acknowledgement; output should preserve source labels.

expected_observable_outcomes: Treats the stated AUROC as weak error discrimination.
Does not treat mean maximum probability as calibration or safe acceptance.
Obtains missing task evidence or routes to review regardless of confidence.
Evaluates repeated voting as a separate policy with correlated-error and full-cost checks.
prohibited_behavior: Accept at a 0.9 confidence threshold.
Equate confidence with calibration.
Claim repeated voting repairs correlated errors.
Skip independent labels or risk-coverage evaluation.
required_evidence: The supplied accuracy, confidence, and AUROC values.
review_criteria: The stated 52.5% accuracy and 0.518 error-detection AUROC indicate weak performance and weak error discrimination on this workload.
Mean maximum probability 0.90 is not evidence of calibration or safe acceptance.
Without evidence for a required case, obtain it or route the case to review regardless of confidence.
A qualification plan needs independent labels, risk-coverage, and accepted-error analysis.
Repeated voting is a separate policy and requires correlated-error and full-cost evaluation.
